questions.q:
What does `document.querySelector('.highlight')` return if there are three `

` elements in the HTML?
questions.a:
It returns only the **first** matching element (the first `

`), not a list. A wrong answer (e.g., "returns all three" or "returns an array") reveals the student confuses `querySelector` (single) with `querySelectorAll` (NodeList of all matches) — a critical distinction because calling `.style.color = 'red'` on a NodeList throws a TypeError.

questions.q:
Explain the difference between `element.innerHTML = 'Bold'` and `element.textContent = 'Bold'` when applied to a `
`.
questions.a: `innerHTML` parses the string as HTML, so the `` tags become actual bold markup — the div will render **Bold**. `textContent` treats the string as literal text, so the user sees the raw characters `Bold` on screen. A wrong answer indicates the student doesn't grasp that `innerHTML` triggers HTML parsing (security risk for user input) while `textContent` is safe for untrusted data — a common board exam trap in "prevent XSS" questions.

questions.q: Write the exact JavaScript statements to: (a) select the `<input id="pincode">`, (b) read its value, (c) create a new `<span>` with class "error" containing "Invalid PIN", and (d) insert it immediately after the input field.
A student writes `document.getElementsByClassName('btn').addEventListener('click', fn)`. Why does this fail, and how would you fix it for all buttons with class "btn"?
questions.a: `getElementsByClassName` returns an **HTMLCollection** (live), not a single element — it has no `addEventListener` method. Fix: use `document.querySelectorAll('.btn').forEach(btn => btn.addEventListener('click', fn))`. A wrong answer (e.g., "use `getElementById` instead") reveals the student doesn't understand that collection-returning methods (`getElementsBy*`, `querySelectorAll`) require iteration, while singleton methods (`getElementById`, `querySelector`) do not — a classic JEE-style "identify the bug" trap.

questions.q: Design a minimal "Aadhaar Masking" feature: an input field where the user types a 12-digit number, and on `blur`, the first 8 digits are replaced with `XXXX XXXX` while the last 4 remain visible. The original value must be stored in a `data-aadhaar` attribute for form submission. Provide the HTML and JavaScript.

Fill in the blank: DOM (Document Object Model) manipulation refers to the process of using JavaScript to ______ access, modify, create, or delete HTML elements and their attributes, styles, and content after the page has loaded, enabling dynamic and interactive web pages.
Fill in the blank: Imagine you are building a "Digital India" ______ portal where citizens report civic issues.
What is DOM (Document Object Model) manipulation? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: DOM (Document Object Model) manipulation refers to the process of using JavaScript to programmatically access, modify, create, or delete HTML elements and their attributes, styles, and content after the page has loaded, enabling dynamic and interactive web pages.

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about DOM (Document Object Model) manipulation?
questions.a: In reality, .style is a CSSStyleDeclaration object — you must set individual properties: el.style.color = 'red'; el.style.fontSize = '18px' (camelCase!).

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to write JavaScript code that selects specific HTML elements using document.getElementById, querySelector, or querySelectorAll, modifies their innerHTML, textContent, style, classList, or attributes, and creates/appends new elements to the DOM in response to user events.
